paragraphs: We are Capital Bancorp, Inc., a bank holding company and a Maryland corporation incorporated in 1998, operating primarily through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Capital Bank, N.A., a commercial-focused community bank based in the Washington, D.C. and Baltimore metropolitan areas. The Bank is headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, received its charter in 1999 and began operations the same year. We serve businesses, not-for-profit associations, entrepreneurs and others throughout the Washington, D.C., Baltimore, other Maryland markets, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, and North Carolina through seven commercial bank branches, one mortgage banking office, three loan production offices, three government loan servicing offices, and one credit card operations office.

On October 1, 2024, the Company completed its acquisition of IFH. At the effective time of the merger, IFH merged with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation in the acquisition. Immediately following the acquisition, West Town Bank & Trust, merged with and into Capital Bank, with Capital Bank as the surviving bank. Windsor Advantage™, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, was acquired in connection with the IFH acquisition.

The Company currently operates four divisions and reporting segments: Commercial Banking, OpenSky™, Windsor Advantage™, and Capital Bank Home Loans ("CBHL"). In determining the appropriateness of segment definition, the Company considers components of the business about which financial information is available and regularly evaluated relative to resource allocation and performance assessment. The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with GAAP, and conform to general practices within the banking industry.

Our Commercial Banking division primarily operates within a corridor extending from Raleigh, North Carolina to Delaware, with significant activity in the Washington, D.C. and Baltimore metropolitan statistical areas. The Commercial Bank also maintains offices in Chicago, Illinois and Fort Lauderdale, Florida. In addition to providing relationship-driven banking services within its primary geographic markets, the Commercial Bank conducts certain lending and deposit activities on a nationwide basis through specialized verticals. These lending verticals include lender finance, government guaranteed lending and other forms of commercial and industrial ("C&I") lending. The Commercial Bank also operates national deposit verticals serving homeowners associations ("HOAs"), title companies, political action committees ("PACs"), not-for-profit organizations, and other commercial clients.

OpenSky™ and CBHL both leverage Capital Bank's national banking charter to operate national consumer business lines. OpenSky™ provides nationwide, digitally-originated and served, secured, partially-secured, and unsecured credit cards to under-banked populations and those looking to rebuild their credit scores. CBHL acts as our residential mortgage origination platform. Windsor Advantage™ generates fee revenue for the Company through its servicing, processing and packaging of SBA and USDA loans for its financial institution clients.

In addition to its subsidiaries discussed above, Capital Bancorp, Inc. owns all of the stock of Capital Bancorp (MD) Statutory Trust I (the "Trust"). The Trust is a special purpose, non-consolidated entity organized for the sole purpose of issuing trust preferred securities.

The Commercial Banking division operates out of seven full service banking locations, three of which are in the Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area ("MSA"), and its full service banking locations in Columbia, Maryland in the Baltimore, Maryland MSA, in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida in the Miami Metro Area MSA, in Chicago, Illinois in the Chicago MSA, and in Raleigh, North Carolina in the Raleigh MSA. Additionally, we have three loan production offices, one located in the Washington, D.C. area, one in Columbia, Maryland, and one in Towson, Maryland. Our Commercial Banking division's commercial loan officers and commercial real estate loan officers provide C&I, commercial real estate, including lender finance loans, and construction lending solutions to business clients in Capital Bank's operating markets.

Government guaranteed lending serves customers throughout the country in need of, and qualifying for, USDA and SBA loans. We generally sell the government guaranteed portion of USDA and SBA loans into the secondary market while retaining the non-guaranteed portion of the loan and the servicing rights. This allows us to realize one time gain on sale income along with a recurring servicing and interest revenue stream. In addition to the business development officers upon whom we rely to generate new business, we also have a dedicated servicing, portfolio management and workout staff with specialized expertise in U.S. government guaranteed loans.

Construction lending is a core competency of our Commercial Banking division. Our construction loan portfolio provides Capital Bank with short duration, higher yield loans. Our construction lending is focused on commercial and residential construction projects within the Washington, D.C. and Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, Maryland metropolitan operating areas, with limited exposure to suburban subdivision tract development.

Lender finance loans are loans to companies used to purchase finance receivables or extend finance receivables to the underlying obligors and are secured primarily by the finance receivables held by our borrowers.

In addition to its loan officers, who have incentives and goals to drive core deposit growth, our Commercial Banking division currently has a team of business development officers concentrating on continuing to diversify and grow Capital Bank's core deposit funding and lessen the dependency on wholesale funding. These officers seek to grow deposits generally across the commercial client customer base and through several specialized deposit channels serving multiple sectors nationwide including the homeowner's association sector, the title insurance sector, political action committees and not-for-profits.

Capital Bank Home Loans ("CBHL") originates conventional and government guaranteed residential mortgage loans on a nationwide basis primarily for sale into the secondary market and, in certain circumstances, for our loan portfolio. Loans sold into the secondary market are sold servicing released. Our residential loan portfolio aims to retain high-quality, lower risk loans which support the Company's business strategies. A portion of the retained residential portfolio is represented by mortgage loans on primary residences within Capital Bank's operating markets to individuals who own businesses where Capital Bank may also pursue a commercial lending relationship and has a vested interest in maintaining the fullest possible banking relationship.

Approximately 78.5% of CBHL loan originations by volume occur within Maryland, Virginia, Delaware and Washington, D.C. The remainder of originations are national in scope and originate primarily through a direct-to-consumer model that utilizes consumer marketing and social media applications.
The OpenSky™ Division provides secured, partially secured and unsecured credit cards on a nationwide basis.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business
As a business operating in the financial services industry, our business and operations may be adversely affected in numerous and complex ways by weak economic conditions.
Our commercial business and operations are concentrated in the greater Washington, D.C. and Baltimore metropolitan areas and we are sensitive to adverse changes in the local economy.
Our customers and businesses in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area may be adversely impacted as a result of the government shutdown and changes in government spending.
We may not be able to measure and limit our credit risk adequately, which could lead to unexpected losses.
Our ACL may prove to be insufficient to absorb life-time losses in our loan portfolio, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
The small- to medium-sized businesses that we lend to may have fewer resources to weather adverse business developments, which may impair our borrowers' ability to repay loans.
Our commercial real estate and real estate construction loan portfolio exposes us to credit risks that may be greater than the risks related to other types of loans.

A portion of our loan portfolio is comprised of commercial loans secured by receivables, inventory, equipment or other commercial collateral, the deterioration in value of which could expose us to credit losses.
A lack of liquidity could impair our ability to fund operations and adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We have several large depositor relationships, the loss of which could force us to fund our business through more expensive and less stable sources.
Our mortgage banking division may not meaningfully contribute to noninterest income.
We earn income by originating residential mortgage loans for resale in the secondary mortgage market, and disruptions in that market could reduce our operating income.
Our financial condition, earnings and asset quality could be adversely affected if we are required to repurchase loans originated for sale by our mortgage banking division.
Delinquencies and credit losses from our OpenSky™ credit card division could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
The inability of our OpenSky™ credit card division to continue its growth rate could adversely affect our earnings.
Our participation in government guaranteed lending activities subjects us to additional risks.
Any modification or reduction in the level of government support for government guaranteed loan programs could result in a significant impact to our results of operations.
Changes to renewable energy tax credits and federal incentive programs could adversely affect certain lending opportunities.
We are subject to interest rate risk as fluctuations in interest rates may adversely affect our earnings.
We could recognize losses on investment securities held in our securities portfolio, particularly if interest rates increase or economic and market conditions deteriorate.
We face strong competition from financial services companies and other companies that offer banking services.
System failure or cybersecurity breaches of our network security could subject us to increased operating costs as well as litigation and other potential losses and regulatory implications.

Failure to maintain an effective system of internal control and disclosure controls and procedures could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and stock price.
Risks Related to Our Operations and the Regulation of Our Industry
Regulatory requirements affecting our loans secured by commercial real estate could limit our ability to leverage our capital and adversely affect our growth and profitability.
Severe weather, earthquakes, other natural disasters, climate change, pandemics, acts of war or terrorism and other external and geopolitical events could significantly impact the business.
The development and use of AI presents risks that may adversely impact our business.
Risks Related to Strategic Growth
A merger or acquisition requires us to make estimates, including the fair value of acquired assets and assumed liabilities.
If our goodwill were determined to be impaired, it could have a negative impact on our profitability.
Acquisitions may disrupt our business.
Risks Related to Ownership of Our Common Stock
The market price of our common stock may be subject to substantial fluctuations, which may make it difficult for you to sell your shares at the volume, prices and times desired.
paragraphs: Ownership of our common stock involves certain risks. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as all other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations. If any of these risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially and adversely affected.

Our performance could be negatively impacted to the extent there is deterioration in business and/or economic conditions, including persistent inflation, supply chain issues or labor shortages, which have direct or indirect impacts on us, our customers and/or our counterparties. All of these factors can individually or in the aggregate be detrimental to our business, and the interplay between these factors can be complex and unpredictable. Adverse economic conditions could have a material, adverse effect on our business, and/or the financial condition of our customers and our results of operations.

Adverse developments affecting financial institutions or the financial services industry generally, such as actual events or concerns involving liquidity, defaults or non-performance, could adversely affect our operations and liquidity.

Actual events involving limited funding liquidity, customer defaults, non-performance or other adverse developments that affect financial institutions or the financial services industry generally, or concerns or rumors about similar events, including the potential negative media coverage, have in the past and may in the future lead to market-wide liquidity problems and erode customer confidence in the banking system. For example, the high-profile bank failures in the first half of 2023 led to volatility and declines in the market for bank stocks and questions about depositor confidence in depository institutions.

Such high-profile bank failures also highlighted the speed at which deposits can be moved in the digital economy, as well as the speed and reach of media attention, including social media, and its ability to disseminate concerns or rumors, in each case potentially exacerbating liquidity concerns. In addition, the banking operating environment and public trading prices of banking institutions can be highly correlated, in particular during times of stress, which could materially and adversely impact the trading price of our common stock and potentially our results of operations.

Additionally, negative news about us or the banking industry in general could negatively impact market and/or customer perceptions of the Company, which could lead to a loss of depositor confidence and an increase in deposit withdrawals, particularly among those with uninsured deposits. Furthermore, the failure of other financial institutions may cause deposit outflows as customers spread deposits among several different banks so as to maximize their amount of FDIC insurance, move deposits to banks deemed "too big to fail" or remove deposits from the banking system entirely. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 40.9% of our deposits were uninsured and 59.1% of our deposits were insured. We rely on these deposits for liquidity. A failure to maintain adequate liquidity could have a material, adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") is intended as a review of significant factors affecting the Company's financial condition and results of operations for the periods indicated. This discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the accompanying consolidated financial statements and the related notes.

This report contains non-GAAP financial measures denoted throughout our MD&A by reference to "non-GAAP." We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to investors because they are used by management to evaluate our operating performance and to make day-to-day operating decisions. In addition, we believe our non-GAAP results in any given reporting period reflect our on-going financial performance in that period and, accordingly, are useful to consider in addition to our GAAP financial results. We further believe the presentation of non-GAAP results increases comparability of period-to-period results.

Other companies may use similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures that may be calculated differently from the way we calculate such measures. Accordingly, our non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similar measures used by such companies. We caution investors not to place undue reliance on such non-GAAP financial measures, but to consider them with the most directly comparable GAAP measures. Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for our results reported under GAAP.
For more information on the computation of non-GAAP financial measures, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliations."
The following summary should be read in conjunction with the MD&A section in its entirety.

Net income of $57.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $26.2 million, or 84.6% when compared to the prior year, augmented in part by the acquisition of IFH and strong organic growth. Net income as adjusted for the year ended December 31, 2025 of $56.3 million excludes the impact of $3.5 million after-tax impact from issuing a call of brokered time deposits acquired from the IFH transaction ("Call of Brokered Time Deposits") and $2.6 million after-tax merger-related expenses. Net income as adjusted for the year ended December 31, 2024 included $3.3 million of after-tax merger-related expenses, $3.2 from the Initial IFH ACL Provision on non-purchased credit deteriorated loans, and $2.6 million of non-recurring equity and debt investment write-down that was nondeductible for tax purposes (non-GAAP). Net interest income of $196.0 million increased $41.2 million from the prior year primarily driven by organic growth and the acquisition of IFH. For more information on the computation of non-GAAP financial measures, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliations."

The net interest margin decreased 12 basis points to 6.10% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 6.22% for the prior year. The decrease was primarily driven by the acquisition of commercial loans from IFH, which diluted the impact from OpenSky™. For the year ended December 31, 2025, average interest earning assets increased $727.9 million, or 29.3%, to $3.2 billion as compared to the same period in 2024, and the average yield on interest earning assets decreased 46 basis points as a result of the acquisition of commercial loans from IFH, diluting the impact from OpenSkyTM. The Commercial Bank net interest margin was 4.38% for the year ended December 31, 2025, which included 15 basis points related to the Call of Brokered Time Deposits, compared to 3.93% for the prior year. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Commercial Bank average interest earning assets increased $713.4 million, or 30.2%, to $3.1 billion as compared to the same period in 2024, driven by the acquired interest-earning assets from IFH and strong organic growth during 2025. The Commercial Bank yield on portfolio loans (non-GAAP, excluding credit card loans) was 6.99% for the year ended December 31, 2025, which included 4 basis points of purchase accounting accretion, compared to 7.03% for the prior year, which included 3 basis points of purchase accounting amortization. Excluding purchase accounting, the Commercial Bank loan yield decreased 11 basis points primarily due to changes in the rate environment. Compared to the same period in the prior year, average interest-bearing liabilities increased $548.7 million, or 35.2%, while the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased 68 basis points to 3.1% from 3.8%. For additional details, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliations."

For the year ended December 31, 2025, the provision for credit losses was $15.0 million, a decrease of $2.8 million from the prior year. The provision for credit losses for the year-ended December 31, 2024 included the initial IFH ACL provision of $4.2 million. Excluding this, the provision for credit losses increased $1.2 million which was primarily due to increased provision expense for OpenSky™ due to growth in the unsecured credit card portfolio. Net charge-offs for the year ended December 31, 2025 were $12.4 million, or 0.45% of average portfolio loans, compared to $9.0 million, or 0.42% of average portfolio loans, for the same period in 2024. The $12.4 million in net charge-offs during the year ended December 31, 2025 were comprised, in part, of OpenSky™ credit card portfolio net charge-offs, with $5.4 million related to unsecured cards and $1.6 million related to secured and partially secured cards. Further, $3.4 million of net charge-offs were related to commercial and industrial loans, $1.9 million were related to owner-occupied commercial real estate loans, and $0.3 million were related to construction loans.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, noninterest income of $49.2 million increased $17.8 million, or 56.6%, from the same period in 2024. This increase was primarily driven by reporting results from the IFH acquisition for a full year in 2025 compared to only three months in 2024. Activity from IFH included increased government loan servicing revenue (Windsor™) of $11.5 million, increased government lending

revenue of $1.9 million, offset by decreased loan servicing rights of $0.5 million. The noninterest income also increased $2.6 million as a result of 2024 including non-recurring equity and debt write-down related to an IFH investment.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, noninterest expense of $155.1 million increased $28.9 million, or 22.9%, from the same period in 2024, largely due to the IFH acquisition. The increase was primarily driven by a $16.1 million, or 28.8%, increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $3.1 million increase in occupancy and equipment, a $3.1 million increase in professional fees, and a $2.1 million, or 7.6%, increase in data processing expense.

Total assets at December 31, 2025 were $3.6 billion, an increase of $399.3 million, or 12.5%, from the balance at December 31, 2024. Net portfolio loans, which exclude mortgage loans held for sale, totaled $3.0 billion at December 31, 2025, an increase of $329.3 million, or 12.5%, compared to $2.6 billion at December 31, 2024. Total liabilities at December 31, 2025 were $3.2 billion, an increase of $352.7 million, or 12.4%, from the balance at December 31, 2024. Total liability growth was primarily due to a $331.3 million increase in deposits and a $28.0 million increase in FHLB advances, partially offset by a decrease in other borrowed funds of $10.0 million when comparing December 31, 2025 to December 31, 2024. Stockholders' equity increased to $401.8 million as of December 31, 2025, compared to $355.1 million at December 31, 2024, or 13.1%.

Deposits were $3.1 billion at December 31, 2025, an increase of $331.3 million or 12.0%, from the balance at December 31, 2024. Average deposits of $2.9 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $711.6 million, or 32.8%, as compared to the prior year. Average noninterest-bearing deposit balances increased $136.4 million to $811.8 million, and represented 28.2% of total average deposits for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to $675.4 million, which represented 31.1% of total average deposits for the prior year.

The Bank's OpenSky™ Division, including shared service and corporate allocations contributed $14.6 million of income before taxes for the year ended December 31, 2025, a decrease of $2.7 million for the segment from the prior year. The $2.7 million decrease was primarily attributable to $1.5 million of increased provision for credit losses, $0.8 million of decreased interest income, and $1.3 million of increased data processing expense related to investments in OpenSky™ initiatives and other investments in technology, partially offset by $1.4 million of increased fee revenue from higher credit card fees. Average OpenSky™ loan balances, net of reserves and deferred fees of $125.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $10.2 million, or 8.9%, as compared to the prior year. OpenSky™ loan balances, net of reserves, of $142.4 million at December 31, 2025 increased by $14.6 million, or 11.5%, compared to $127.8 million at December 31, 2024. Corresponding non-interest bearing deposit balances of $163.2 million at December 31, 2025 decreased $3.2 million, or 4.3%, compared to $166.4 million at December 31, 2024. Gross unsecured loan balances of $61.4 million at December 31, 2025 increased $18.9 million, or 44.7%, compared to $42.4 million at December 31, 2024. For the year ended December 31, 2025, noninterest income of $17.4 million increased $1.3 million due primarily to higher credit-card related fees.

paragraphs: 本公司為 Capital Bancorp, Inc.，為一家銀行控股公司，並為一間於 1998 年在馬裏蘭州註冊成立的公司，主要透過我們 100%  owned 的子公司 Capital Bank, N.A. 進行營運，該子公司為一家以商業為導向的社區銀行，位於華盛頓特區及巴爾的摩都會區。該銀行總部設於馬裏蘭州洛克維爾市，於 1999 年取得執照並開始營運。我們服務華盛頓特區、巴爾的摩、其他馬裏蘭州市場、特拉華州、佛羅裏達州、伊利諾州及北卡羅來納州的企業、非營利協會、創業者及其他人士，透過七家商業銀行分行、一家房貸銀行辦公室、三家貸款業務辦公室、三家政府貸款服務辦公室及一家信用卡業務辦公室。
於 2024 年 10 月 1 日，本公司完成對 IFH 的收購。在合併生效時，IFH 合併進本公司，本公司繼續為收購後的存續公司。收購後立即，West Town Bank & Trust 合併進 Capital Bank，Capital Bank 為存續銀行。Windsor Advantage™，為本公司 100%  owned 的子公司，係於 IFH 收購時一併取得。
本公司目前運作四個部門及應報告分部：商業銀行、OpenSky™、Windsor Advantage™ 及 Capital Bank Home Loans（"CBHL"）。在決定分部定義是否適當時，本公司考量業務中可取得財務資訊的組成部分，並定期評估資源配置及績效評估。隨附的合併財務報表係根據 GAAP 會計準則編製，並符合銀行業的一般慣例。

我們的商業銀行部門主要運作於從北卡羅來納州 Raleigh 至特拉華州的走廊地區，並在華盛頓特區及巴爾的摩都會區有大量業務活動。商業銀行亦在伊利諾州芝加哥及佛羅裏達州 Fort Lauderdale 設有分行。除了在主要地理市場提供以關係為導向的銀行服務外，商業銀行亦透過專門垂直部門，在全國範圍內進行貸款及存款業務。這些貸款垂直部門包括貸款金融、政府擔保貸款及其他形式的商業及工業（"C&I"）貸款。商業銀行亦運作全國性存款垂直部門，服務住宅協會（"HOAs"）、地產公司、政治行動委員會（"PACs"）、非營利組織及其他商業客戶。

OpenSky™ 及 CBHL 都利用 Capital Bank 的全國性銀行執照運作全國性消費者業務線。OpenSky™ 提供全國範圍內、透過數位方式發行及服務的 secured、partially-secured 及 unsecured 信用卡，服務信用不足的人羣及希望重建信用分數的客戶。CBHL 作為我們的住宅房貸發行平台。Windsor Advantage™ 透過為其金融機構客戶處理、處理及打包 SBA 及 USDA 貸款的服務，為本公司產生費用收入。
除了上述子公司外，Capital Bancorp, Inc. 還擁有 Capital Bancorp (MD) Statutory Trust I（"Trust"）全部股票。Trust 為一間專門用途、非合併的實體，成立目的 solely 為發行信託優先股。

商業銀行部門運作於七家全功能銀行分行，其中三家位於華盛頓特區都會區（"MSA"），另外三家分別位於馬裏蘭州 Columbia、佛羅裏達州 Ft. Lauderdale（屬於邁阿密都會區 MSA）、伊利諾州芝加哥（屬於芝加哥 MSA）及北卡羅來納州 Raleigh（屬於 Raleigh MSA）。此外，我們還設有三家貸款業務辦公室，分別位於華盛頓特區地區、馬裏蘭州 Columbia 及馬裏蘭州 Towson。我們商業銀行部門的商業貸款經理及商業不動產貸款經理，為 Capital Bank 運作市場中的企業客戶提供 C&I、商業不動產貸款（包括貸款金融貸款）及建設貸款解決方案。
政府擔保貸款服務全國各地需要且符合 USDA 及 SBA 貸款條件的客戶。我們通常將 USDA 及 SBA 貸款的政府擔保部分出售至次級市場，同時保留貸款的非擔保部分及服務權。這使我們能實現一次過銷售收益，並有持續的服務及利息收入流。除了我們依賴的業務開發經理來產生新業務外，我們還擁有專門的服務、投資組合管理及處置團隊，具備美國政府擔保貸款的專業知識。
Construction lending 是本公司商業銀行部門的核心專長。我們的建設貸款組合為 Capital Bank 提供短週期、高報酬的貸款。我們的建設貸款業務聚焦於華盛頓特區以及巴爾的摩-哥倫比亞-陶森，馬裏蘭州都會區的商業及住宅建設項目，並對郊區 subdivision tract 開發的敞口有限。
Lender finance loans 是提供給公司的貸款，用以購買或延伸財務應收款至基礎債務人，並主要以借款人持有的財務應收款作為擔保。
除了貸款經理，他們有激勵措施與目標以推動核心存款成長，本公司商業銀行部門目前還有一支業務發展團隊，專注於持續多元化與成長 Capital Bank 的核心存款資金，並減少對 wholesale 資金的依賴。這些經理致力於在商業客戶基礎上廣泛成長存款，並透過多個專門存款渠道服務全國多個產業，包括房東協會產業、房貸保險產業、政治行動委員會及非營利組織。

Capital Bank Home Loans ("CBHL") 在全國範圍內發放傳統及政府擔保的住宅房貸，主要為銷售至次級市場，並在特定情況下為本公司貸款組合。銷售至次級市場的貸款為售出並解除服務權。我們的住宅貸款組合旨在保留高品質、低風險貸款，以支持本公司的業務策略。保留的住宅貸款組閤中，一部分為 Capital Bank 操作市場內個人的住宅房貸，這些個人擁有企業，本公司可能同時追求商業貸款關係，並有興趣維持最完整的銀行關係。
約 78.5% 的 CBHL 貸款發放量發生在馬裏蘭州、維吉尼亞州、特拉華州及華盛頓特區。其餘的貸款發放為全國範圍，主要透過直接對消費者模式進行，並利用消費者行銷及社交媒體應用程式。
OpenSky™ 分部提供全國範圍的擔保貸款、部分擔保貸款及無擔保信用卡。

paragraphs: 本項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」（"MD&A"）旨在回顧影響本公司財務狀況與營運成果之重大因素，針對所列期間。本項討論與分析應與附屬財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。
本報告包含非GAAP財務指標，於本MD&A中以"non-GAAP"標示。我們認為這些非GAAP財務指標對投資人而言提供有用的資訊，因其為管理層評估營運績效及進行日常營運決策所使用。此外，我們認為本公司在任一報告期間的非GAAP結果反映該期間持續的財務表現，因此與GAAP財務結果一併考量是有用的。我們進一步認為，呈現非GAAP結果可提高各期間結果的可比性。
其他公司可能使用相同標題的非GAAP財務指標，但計算方式可能與本公司不同。因此，本公司非GAAP財務指標可能與這些公司使用的類似指標不具可比性。我們提醒投資人不要過度依賴這些非GAAP財務指標，應與最直接對應的GAAP財務指標一併考量。非GAAP財務指標作為分析工具有其限制，不應孤立使用或作為GAAP財務結果的替代。
如需瞭解非GAAP財務指標的計算方式，請參閱「非GAAP財務指標與重編表」。
以下摘要應與MD&A部分完整內容一併閱讀。

2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度淨收入為 57.2 百萬美元，較前一年增加 26.2 百萬美元，或成長 84.6%，部分原因係因取得 IFH 以及強勁的內生成長。2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度調整後淨收入為 56.3 百萬美元，排除因發行來自 IFH 交易取得的經紀時間存款的呼籲（"Call of Brokered Time Deposits"）所產生的 3.5 百萬美元稅後影響，以及 2.6 百萬美元稅後併購相關費用。2024 年 12 月 31 日會計年度調整後淨收入包含 3.3 百萬美元稅後併購相關費用、3.2 百萬美元來自初始 IFH ACL 提列對非購入信用惡化貸款的準備金，以及 2.6 百萬美元非經常性權益及債務投資減損，該減損於稅務上不可扣抵（非 GAAP）。2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度淨利息收入為 196.0 百萬美元，較前一年增加 41.2 百萬美元，主要因內生成長及取得 IFH。如需更多關於非 GAAP 財務指標計算的資訊，請參閱 "Non-GAAP 財務指標與重複明細"。

2025年12月31日財年淨利息邊際率下降12個基點至6.10%，較前一年的6.22%為低。此下降主要因取得IFH的商業貸款，稀釋了OpenSky™的影響。2025年12月31日財年平均利息收入資產增加727.9 百萬美元，或成長29.3%，達32 億美元，較2024年同期增加，而平均利息收入資產收益率下降46個基點，因取得IFH的商業貸款，稀釋了OpenSky™的影響。2025年12月31日財年商業銀行淨利息邊際率為4.38%，其中包含15個基點與Call of Brokered Time Deposits相關，較前一年的3.93%為高。2025年12月31日財年商業銀行平均利息收入資產增加713.4 百萬美元，或成長30.2%，達31 億美元，較2024年同期增加，因取得IFH的利息收入資產及2025年強勁的內生成長所致。2025年12月31日財年商業銀行貸款收益率（非GAAP，排除信用卡貸款）為6.99%，其中包含4個基點的購入資產攤銷收益，較前一年的7.03%為低，其中包含3個基點的購入資產攤銷費用。排除購入資產後，商業銀行貸款收益率下降11個基點，主要因利率環境的變化。與前一年同期相比，平均利息負債增加548.7 百萬美元，或成長35.2%，而平均利息負債成本下降68個基點至3.1%，較前一年的3.8%為低。如需更多細節，請參閱「非GAAP財務指標與重編表」。

2025年12月31日財年信貸減損撥備為15.0 百萬美元，較前一年減少2.8 百萬美元。2024年12月31日財年信貸減損撥備包含初始IFH ACL撥備4.2 百萬美元。扣除此部分後，信貸減損撥備增加1.2 百萬美元，主要因OpenSky™的信貸減損費用因未secured信用卡組合成長而增加。2025年12月31日財年淨信貸減損為12.4 百萬美元，或平均貸款組合的0.45%，較2024年同期的9.0 百萬美元，或平均貸款組合的0.42%為高。2025年12月31日財年12.4 百萬美元淨信貸減損包含部分OpenSky™信用卡組合的淨信貸減損，其中5.4 百萬美元與未secured信用卡相關，1.6 百萬美元與secured及部分secured信用卡相關。此外，3.4 百萬美元淨信貸減損與商業及工業貸款相關，1.9 百萬美元與所有權人佔有商業不動產貸款相關，0.3 百萬美元與建設貸款相關。
營業收入為 1.9 百萬美元，抵銷因貸款服務權減少 0.5 百萬美元。非利息收入亦因 2024 年包括與 IFH 投資相關的非經常性權益及債務減損而增加 2.6 百萬美元。

截至2025年12月31日止年度，非利息費用為155.1 百萬美元，較2024年同期增加28.9 百萬美元，或22.9%，主要係因IFH收購所致。此增加主要為 salaries and employee benefits 增加16.1 百萬美元，或28.8%，occupancy and equipment 增加3.1 百萬美元，professional fees 增加3.1 百萬美元，以及 data processing expense 增加2.1 百萬美元，或7.6%。

2025 年 12 月 31 日總資產為 3.6 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的資產數額增加 399.3 百萬美元，增幅為 12.5%。扣除持有待售房貸貸款後的淨貸款組合，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 3.0 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 2.6 十億美元增加 329.3 百萬美元，增幅為 12.5%。2025 年 12 月 31 日總負債為 3.2 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的負債數額增加 352.7 百萬美元，增幅為 12.4%。總負債增加主要係因存款增加 331.3 百萬美元，以及 FHLB 借款增加 28.0 百萬美元，部分抵銷因其他借款減少 10.0 百萬美元的影響。2025 年 12 月 31 日股東權益為 401.8 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 355.1 百萬美元增加 13.1%。
存款於2025年12月31日為3.1十億美元，較2024年12月31日的餘額增加331.3百萬美元，或12.0%。2025年12月31日財年平均存款為2.9十億美元，較前一財年增加711.6百萬美元，或32.8%。平均非利息存款餘額增加136.4百萬美元至811.8百萬美元，佔2025年12月31日財年總平均存款的28.2%，較前一財年675.4百萬美元，佔總平均存款的31.1%。

銀行的OpenSky™部門，包括共享服務及企業分配，於2025年12月31日止年度產生稅前收入14.6百萬美元，較前一年度該部門減少2.7百萬美元。減少2.7百萬美元主要係因信貸損失撥備增加1.5百萬美元、利息收入減少0.8百萬美元，以及與OpenSky™投資及其它科技投資相關的資料處理費用增加1.3百萬美元，部分抵銷因信用卡費用增加而產生的費用收入增加1.4百萬美元。2025年12月31日止年度，扣除撥備及遞延費用後的OpenSky™貸款餘額為125.8百萬美元，較前一年度增加10.2百萬美元，或8.9%。OpenSky™貸款餘額，扣除撥備後為142.4百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的127.8百萬美元增加14.6百萬美元，或11.5%。對應的非利息存款餘額為163.2百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的166.4百萬美元減少3.2百萬美元，或4.3%。未擔保貸款餘額為61.4百萬美元，較2024年12月31日的42.4百萬美元增加18.9百萬美元，或44.7%。2025年12月31日止年度，非利息收入為17.4百萬美元，較前一年度增加1.3百萬美元，主要係因信用卡相關費用增加。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
作為營運於金融服務業的企業，本公司業務及營運可能因經濟條件惡化而以多種複雜方式受到不利影響。
本公司商業業務及營運主要集中於華盛頓特區及巴爾的摩都會區，因此對當地經濟的不利變動較為敏感。
華盛頓特區都會區的客戶及業務可能因政府停擺及政府支出變動而受到不利影響。
本公司可能無法充分衡量並控制信用風險，這可能會導致意外損失。
本公司信貸減值準備（ACL）可能證明不足以吸收貸款組閤中的長期損失，這可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司所貸款予的中小企業可能擁有較少資源應對不利的業務發展，這可能會影響借款人償還貸款的能力。
本公司商業不動產及不動產建設貸款組合使本公司面臨較其他類型貸款更高的信用風險。
本公司貸款組閤中有一部分為以應收款、存貨、設備或其他商業擔保品為抵押的商業貸款，這些資產價值惡化可能使本公司面臨信用損失風險。
流動性不足可能影響本公司資金運作的能力，並對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司擁有數個大型存款客戶關係，若失去這些客戶關係，可能迫使本公司透過成本較高且較不穩定的來源來資助業務。
本公司房貸銀行部門可能無法對非利息收入產生顯著貢獻。
本公司透過發放住宅房貸貸款並轉售至次級房貸市場來獲取收入，若該市場出現動盪，可能降低本公司營運收入。
若本公司被要求回購由房貸銀行部門發放並用以銷售的貸款，可能對本公司財務狀況、獲利能力及資產品質產生不利影響。
OpenSky™信用卡部門的逾期帳款及信用損失可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
若OpenSky™信用卡部門無法持續維持其成長速度，可能對本公司獲利能力產生不利影響。
本公司參與政府保證貸款業務，可能面臨額外風險。
若政府對政府保證貸款計畫的支援程度有所修改或減少，可能會對本公司營運成果產生重大影響。
可再生能源稅額抵減及聯邦激勵計畫的變動，可能對某些貸款機會產生不利影響。
本公司面臨利率風險，因利率波動可能對本公司獲利產生不利影響。
本公司可能在所持有證券投資組閤中的投資證券認列損失，特別是在利率上升或經濟與市場條件惡化的情況下。
本公司面臨來自金融服務公司及其他提供銀行服務公司的強烈競爭。
本公司網路安全系統故障或網路安全遭駭客入侵，可能導致營運成本增加，以及訴訟及其他潛在損失與監管後果。
若無法維持有效的內部控制制度及揭露控制與程序，可能對本公司營運成果、財務狀況及股票價格產生重大不利影響。
與我們營運及產業監管相關的風險
影響我們以商業不動產擔保貸款的監管要求，可能限制我們運用資本的能力，並對我們的成長與獲利產生不利影響。
嚴峻天氣、地震、其他天然災害、氣候變遷、疫情、戰爭行為或恐怖攻擊等其他外部及地緣政治事件，可能對營運產生重大影響。
人工智慧的發展與應用，可能帶來風險，對我們的業務產生不利影響。
與戰略成長相關的風險
併購或收購需要我們做出估計，包括取得資產與承擔負債的公允價值。
若我們的商譽被判定為減損，可能對我們的獲利產生負面影響。
收購可能幹擾我們的業務
與本公司普通股 ownership 相關的風險
本公司普通股的市場價格可能出現顯著波動，這可能會使您難以在 desired 的成交量、價格和時間出售您的股份
paragraphs: 本公司普通股的持有涉及某些風險。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。您應謹慎考量下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中包含的所有其他資訊。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務運作。若任何這些風險實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們的表現可能因商業與/或經濟條件惡化而受到負面影響，包括持續的通貨膨脹、供應鏈問題或勞動力短缺，這些因素可能對我們、我們的客戶與/或交易對手產生直接或間接的影響。所有這些因素，無論個別或整體，都可能對我們的業務造成不利影響，而這些因素之間的相互作用可能複雜且難以預測。不利的經濟條件可能對我們的業務，以及我們客戶的財務狀況與我們的營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
影響金融機構或金融服務產業的不利發展，例如實際發生或存在的流動性問題、違約或未履行義務等情況，可能對我們的營運與流動性造成不利影響。
實際發生涉及有限流動性資金、客戶違約、未履行義務或其他影響金融機構或金融服務產業的不利發展，或對類似事件的擔憂或流言，包括潛在的負面媒體報導，過去曾導致市場範圍的流動性問題，並削弱銀行體系的客戶信心。例如，2023年上半年的知名銀行倒閉事件導致銀行股市場波動與下跌，並引發對存款人對存款機構信心的質疑。
這些知名銀行倒閉事件也突顯了在數位經濟中存款可以迅速轉移的速度，以及媒體關注的速度與範圍，包括社交媒體，其傳播擔憂或流言的能力，每種情況都可能加劇流動性問題。此外，在壓力時期，銀行營運環境與銀行機構的公開交易價格可能高度相關，這可能對本公司普通股的交易價格造成重大且不利的影響，並可能影響我們的營運成果。

此外，關於本公司或金融產業的負面新聞可能影響市場與/或客戶對本公司的看法，這可能導致存款人信心下降，並增加存款提款，特別是在那些未受FDIC保險的存款人中。此外，其他金融機構的失敗可能導致存款流出，因為客戶會將存款分散至多家銀行，以最大化其FDIC保險金額，將存款轉移到被認為"太大而無法倒閉"的銀行，或完全從銀行體系中撤出存款。截至2025年12月31日，本公司約40.9%的存款為未受保險，59.1%的存款為受保險。我們依賴這些存款來維持流動性。若無法維持足夠的流動性，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
